newsitem.title: FRANCE: Portugal not for EMU flexibility, bar debt -paper.
newsitem.headline: Portugal not for EMU flexibility, bar debt -paper.

text.p: Portugal does not favour flexible interpretation of the Maastricht treaty EMU criteria, except on debt, State Secretary for the Treasury and Finance Fernando Teixera Dos Santos said in a newspaper interview published on Thursday.
"Except for the one on public debt, we are not in favour of a flexible approach to the criteria," he was quoted as telling the French business daily La Tribune.
The state secretary underlined again his country's position that it should be considered on its own merits for European monetary union.
"Our number one trading partner is not Spain, it's Germany," he said.

"We obviously want all countries from the south to be part of the single currency. But whatever happens, if Portugal is ready, as we believe, it will be in the euro, even if it has to be the only Mediterranean country allowed in in 1999," he said.
Portugal's stance against flexible reading of the Maastricht treaty economic fitness criteria was "because the euro has to be a strong and credible currency", he said.

He said this did not mean Portugal was not open to talks with its partners when EMU selection time arrived next year but he added: "I don't think it serves any purpose to give oneself room for manoeuvre on goals which we are supposed to achieve".
